capabilities: Set default highlight languages per file, folder, or vault with priority fallback
Apply standalone offline color themes (One Dark Pro, Dracula, Nord, etc.) to code, fixed or following light/dark mode
Recognize exercise code in note text without backticks for configured files or folders
Render text code blocks as Markdown content via language replacement rules
Add rule-setting entries to Notebook Navigator file and folder context menus
disambiguation: Not a command palette or code formatter; it only changes how code is displayed with syntax highlighting themes and language rules.
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Requires Obsidian 1.8.0 or newer; mobile is untested. ZIP install path is described in detail while the plugin awaits full directory sync. Provides highlighting only, no code execution or semantic coloring, and blocks over 200,000 characters keep native rendering.
problem: Obsidian's code highlighting depends on explicit language tags and the global theme, leaving untagged inline code and code blocks plain and offering no per-file color control.

relations.evidence: supports stable reading/editing and Notebook Navigator menus

summary: Syntax-highlighting theme plugin that applies per-file, folder, or vault language rules and standalone color themes to inline code, tables, and code blocks.
